output.brief: Don't roll back gateway 5.8. The latency regression comes from the 2 Nov storage compaction tuning change, not the gateway. Per-cell data shows every cell that received the compaction push (FC-7710) jumped to about 300 ms within minutes. aps-3, which skipped the push but did get 5.8, stayed at 94 ms. A test rollback of euw-1 to 5.7 changed nothing (291 → 297 → 293 ms). Storage nodes after the push show compaction at 6 threads, disk at 97% utilisation, read queue wait of 205 ms, and node-side GET time up from 61 to 262 ms. Network and traffic growth don't fit the timing. A rollback would take about 4 hours and would reopen the signature vulnerability (SEC-2291) without fixing latency. Next step: revert the compaction change in one cell first (aps-3 is the control), watch p99 and backlog, then extend to the other cells. Don't pause compaction fleet-wide. Backlog is 11.2% and nearing the 15% danger point, so monitor it, and revisit Orrin rate limiting if backlog nears 15%. Backlog growth sources are not yet attributed (job reports 10 Nov). Confidence is high on the cause, moderate on backlog origin.
